items.title: Show HN: I built a blind taste test for Claude and Codex designs
items.why_it_matters: An indie developer built and shipped a blind taste-test website comparing landing pages generated by Claude and Codex. It is a clean, simple side project built using your exact stack that went live and gathered real feedback. You can run through the taste test this week to see which model's design patterns you prefer, and then copy those prompting styles to build your next Next.js page.

items.title: I was paying too much for Claude and codex here is how I reduced 90% of it
items.why_it_matters: A developer released Qarinah, an open-source tool designed to drastically cut down on API costs when using Claude and Codex for coding. Since you are actively building with these tools, managing token spend is the easiest way to keep your project viable. You can clone the Qarinah repository this week and run it locally to see if it reduces your API bill on your next AI-ingest commit.

items.title: Introducing Claude Opus 5
items.why_it_matters: Anthropic has officially introduced Claude Opus 5, their latest high-tier model. It brings massive upgrades to reasoning and code generation, which will directly impact how well your AI assistant handles complex state management and database schemas. You can try switching your Claude Code or Codex CLI settings to use the Opus 5 model this week to help you refactor your Supabase integration.

items.title: Show HN: Sync Claude Code and Codex configs, with a board that shows the drift
items.why_it_matters: This new open-source manager lets you sync your configurations between Claude Code and Codex, complete with a dashboard that highlights any settings drift. It solves the headache of manually maintaining separate system prompts and rules across your two primary coding tools. You can install the package this week and run it to instantly align your custom instructions across both environments.

items.title: Claude Code Lightbar for Mac OS
items.why_it_matters: This is a lightweight macOS status bar utility specifically for monitoring your Claude Code background processes. It gives you a quick, glanceable way to see what your terminal agent is doing without having to keep your terminal window in focus constantly. You can download the app from the repository this week and run it to streamline your multitasking while building.
